title: Tamara
summary: A poster that treats holiday greetings the way Calvino treats signs, as things you read long before you understand them.
coverAlt: Red poster with twelve hand-lettered holiday greetings arranged in a circle

blocks.heading: The brief
blocks.body: Choose one city from Italo Calvino’s *Invisible Cities* and translate its language into a visual form. Not an illustration of the city, but a system that behaves the way the city behaves.

blocks.heading: The city
blocks.body:
In Tamara, the traveler never sees things, only signs of things. A pair of tongs stands for the dentist. A tankard stands for the tavern. You leave the city without ever discovering it.

I wanted a poster that works the same way, where words turn into signs before they turn into meaning.

blocks.label: Research wall. Photos of storefront signs, greeting cards and calligraphy samples collected in week one.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body:
I started with the most automatic phrases I know, the greetings we write on cards without thinking. Happy Birthday. Happy New Year. Merry Christmas.

I redrew each one by hand until it stopped looking like a word and started looking like an emblem. Arranged in a circle, the twelve greetings become a calendar you have to decode.

blocks.caption: Lettering iterations. Replace with three rounds of one greeting moving from legible to symbolic.

blocks.alt: Close-up of the circular arrangement of lettered greetings
blocks.caption: Each greeting is drawn as one continuous sign.

blocks.alt: Small passage of text along the bottom of the poster
blocks.caption: Calvino’s passage runs along the bottom, small enough that only someone who stops will read it.

blocks.text: I wanted the words to arrive before their meaning does.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body:
The red ground came late. Earlier versions in black felt like a diagram. Red made it feel like a holiday card, and that made the idea land.

Next time I would test the poster with people who don’t read English, to see whether the signs hold up without the words.
